subject: Model Omega-2b p95 drift — request provisional intervention & rollback-guard
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Metric alert — p95 drift observed on model-omega-2b (hotpath)

Team,

Monitoring picked up a sustained p95 latency increase for model-omega-2b starting ~07:40 PDT. Summary:
- Window: 07:40 - 08:05 PDT
- p95 baseline: ~220ms -> current: ~810ms
- Error rate stable (0.3%), but tail latency is client-impacting for streaming hotpath traffic

I've attached an evidence pack with slow traces and a short query snippet showing the request distribution. No obvious infra OOMs or GPU saturation in the first sweep; appears correlated with a kernel selection path change tied to the quantized runtime for omega-2b.

Asking for quick triage: can infra/runtime confirm whether this aligns with yesterday's kernel roll?

Attachments: evidence_pack_omega2b.zip, query_snippet_omega2b.log

- Monica
Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@techharbor.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Metric alert — p95 drift observed on model-omega-2b (hotpath)

Thanks Monica — I reviewed the evidence pack. This looks customer affecting for TechHarbor (high-traffic hotpath).

Ask: I want a provisional mitigation plan we can authorize quickly:
1) Controlled traffic fencing (route new sessions to omega-2a fallback for identified TechHarbor API keys)
2) Short-duration provisional throttle (reduce concurrency for omega-2b by 40%)
3) Preventive rollback guard (do not auto-update the kernel selection on the pool serving omega-2b until we confirm fix)

Kimberly/Karthik/Marcus — please advise feasibility and estimated blast radius for 1–3.

Alyssa — looping you here so TechHarbor ops has visibility. If you can confirm whether immediate fallback to omega-2a is acceptable while we investigate, that will help the decision.

I attached a quick sketch of the proposed steps (provisional-plan-v1.pdf). If we agree, I'll sign off to enact provisional controls and request a temporary SLA carveout for the next 6 hours while we triage.

- Grace
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Metric alert — p95 drift observed on model-omega-2b (hotpath)

Quick feasibility note:
- Traffic fencing by API key: doable. We can add a routing rule in the smart-router to pin TechHarbor production keys to omega-2a within ~12 minutes. Impact: additional cost to TechHarbor (2x tokens while on fallback) and temporary capacity pressure on omega-2a pool.
- Provisional throttle: we can apply a concurrency cap via rate-limiter/route policy immediately; 40% reduction is conservative and safe.
- Rollback guard: set an activation hold on kernel-autoselect for the node pool; this is a config flip and low-risk.

Proposed immediate actions (if Grace approves):
1) Pin TechHarbor production keys to omega-2a (12 min)
2) Apply 40% concurrency cap on omega-2b for 4 hours (will auto-lift unless extended)
3) Add rollback-guard tag to omega-2b pool config and notify kernel team

I'll prepare the exact command snippets and a short runbook. Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@techharbor.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@techharbor.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Metric alert — p95 drift observed on model-omega-2b (hotpath)

Grace / team,

Thanks for the quick heads-up. We're seeing increased callback latency and a small but visible drop in conversion rates on our payments hotpath — impact window aligns with your metrics. Immediate fallback to omega-2a is acceptable from our side; it will slightly increase costs but preserves UX.

Request from TechHarbor: please include an explicit SLA note and a post-incident summary we can share with our leadership. Also confirm whether you will trigger the rollback-guard or whether you plan a code/kernel revert. Our contracts team (cc'd) will want the temporary SLA carveout documented.

Alyssa
Ops Lead, TechHarbor
alyssa@techharbor.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@techharbor.com>, contracts@techharbor.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Metric alert — p95 drift observed on model-omega-2b (hotpath)

Approved. Per Marcus's plan, run the steps in order and copy me on live updates:
- Pin TechHarbor prod keys -> omega-2a (execute now)
- Apply 40% concurrency cap on omega-2b (4-hour window)
- Add rollback-guard tag to omega-2b pool config (do not auto-apply kernel changes)

Operational notes:
- I'll sign a provisional SLA carveout for a 6-hour window (documented) and send the DocuSign link to TechHarbor contracts.
- Monica: collect traces and a short MEP (minimal evidence pack) for TechHarbor leadership.
- Marcus: prepare rollback runbook and a safe re-introduction plan for omega-2b once kernel patch is validated.

DocuSign (provisional carveout): https://docusign.com/s/tp-approve-fallback
Incident ticket created: INF-20250715-9821

Thanks team — let's keep comms tight.

- Grace
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
